e.note: Best: A3 at 24.7% reach vs 6.6% for the benchmark

e.text: A3 leads at 24.7% vs benchmark 6.6%; asking the Critic how to push further.

e.note: Reading results for A3, A1, A2

critique.summary: Citywide targeted social ($7560, ~525-535 adopters in every plan), NPB co-branded drops ($2000, 351–386 adopters) and baseball podcast reads ($2500–3400, ~170 each) drive results, and A3 stacks all three to 24.7% reach (P10 23.5%), well ahead of A1, A2 and the 6.6% benchmark. Zone-level spend does not pay: pop-ups ($2500 for 11–40 adopters), street teams ($450 for 7–14) and zone social ads ($2520 for 27–28) barely move the needle, and A3's are scheduled on days 38–40, too late for word of mouth to spread.

findings.finding: Best on every measure: 24.7% reach (P10 23.5%) with 3638 adopters at $6.69 each, and 54.7% word of mouth; the Hanshin Tigers drop (386 for $2000) and two podcasts (171 and 170) carry it.
Late street teams on days 38–40 in zones 3, 0 and 4 credited only 7–10 adopters per $450, and social:0 in Kagurazaka 4 drew 27 adopters for $2520.

Reach 21.8% (P10 20.6%) at $7.03 per adopter; the Orix drop (362) and R2C2 read (173) work, but the naoto.K pop-up on day 40 got 11 adopters for $2500 and the four Kagurazaka street teams got 9–11 each.

Weakest plan at 20.7% reach and $7.73 per adopter; the Ginza–Aoyama focus lifted Drag Race and Lululemon to 30.4%, but Gaming and sports stars fell to 10.5%, and the MoonFlower pop-up returned only 15 adopters for $2500.
Only 6.6% reach at $13.2 per adopter with $12760 spent, so every taste-driven plan roughly triples reach at about half the cost per adopter.

changes.change: Start from A3 and add a second NPB co-branded drop (Orix Buffaloes from A1 or Chiba Lotte Marines from A2) alongside the Hanshin Tigers collab, running days 0–42.
changes.why: Each drop credited 351–386 adopters for $2000, by far the best yield on the menu.

changes.change: Add the Players' Tribune R2C2 read from A1 (podcast CA1B77AE) on about day 4, alongside the existing day 5 and day 20 reads.
changes.why: It credited 173 adopters for $2500, cheaper than A3's existing reads, and early placement feeds word of mouth.

changes.change: Cut A3's social:0 Kagurazaka 4 ads ($2520) and the four day 38–40 street teams (street:1, street:3, street:0, street:4; $1800 total).
changes.why: Together they credited only about 60 adopters for $4320, and late street days leave no time for word of mouth.

changes.change: Keep a single pop-up, but move the Sagaya Ginza popup:A3B42C26 from day 40 to about day 20–25.
changes.why: Pop-ups yield 11–40 adopters for $2500, and a mid-run date gives word of mouth time to spread before launch.

e.note: Citywide targeted social ($7560, ~525-535 adopters in every plan), NPB co-branded drops ($2000, 351–386 adopters) and baseball podcast reads ($2500–3400, ~170 each) drive results, and A3 stacks all three to 24.7% reach (P10 23.5%), well ahead of A1, A2 and the 6.6% benchmark. Zone-level spend does not pay: pop-ups ($2500 for 11–40 adopters), street teams ($450 for 7–14) and zone social ads ($2520 for 27–28) barely move the needle, and A3's are scheduled on days 38–40, too late for word of mouth to spread.

e.text: Applying the Critic: more NPB team drops and podcasts, cut weak street teams, move the Ginza pop-up earlier.

e.note: Revising: Start from A3: add a second NPB drop (Orix or Chiba Lotte), add early R2C2 Players' Tribune read ~day 4, cut Kagurazaka zone ads and late street teams, move the Sagaya Ginza pop-up to day 20–25. One version with two drops, one with three drops if budget allows.

strategies.name: Media pull, all-partner network
strategies.thesis: Use the three things that drive results (citywide ads, the Hanshin Tigers drop at 0.96 affinity, and two early Yamamoto/Dodgers-driven podcast reads at 0.90–0.91) to spread word of mouth early, then let all 16 partner venues (each 0.93–0.95 affinity, pulled in by Ohtani and the Giants, about 20–25 adopters per $300) and a mid-run Sagaya Ginza pop-up turn that reach into visits. Estimated 29.7% reach and 4,365 adopters, against A3's 3,638.

e.text: B1 reaches 30.6% of fans, nearly 5x the 6.6% benchmark, at $5.44 per fan.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B1

plan.headline: Dodgers Ohtani Pop-Up Tokyo: projected 30.6% reach (29.2–32.2%), ~4,500 adopters for $24,510
plan.summary: We bet on early media pull from citywide social ads, a Hanshin Tigers co-branded drop (0.96 affinity) and two Yamamoto/Dodgers-driven podcast reads, then convert that reach through 16 partner venues and a Sagaya Ginza pop-up. Qloo taste data shows this crowd over-indexes heavily on these brands, shows and venues (0.90–0.96 affinity), which is why the simulation credits word of mouth with 60% of adoption. Expect about 4,506 adopters at $5.44 each versus 967 for a same-budget foot-traffic plan, but this is a simulation built on Qloo taste data, not a guarantee.
